---
title: "Economic freedom bound to public good"
description: "As liberal-democratic principle"
order: 17
status: "draft"
---

## Aspects and tensions

property as a check on state power (economic independence enabling political dissent) vs. property as entrenching pre-existing inequality into political influence (money in politics, oligarchic capture — tying back to the political-equality principle); social-market economy vs. laissez-faire vs. socialist-democratic models as different resolutions of the freedom/public-good balance; expropriation and compensation law (when can the state take property, and on what terms — Art. 14(3) GG as a case study); the welfare state as the institutional mechanism binding markets to public good (redistribution, regulation); economic democracy debates (co-determination/Mitbestimmung — should workers have governance rights in firms, not just political ones); Piketty-style debates on whether extreme wealth concentration is itself a threat to political equality and democratic legitimacy.
